text: One of the most noteworthy discoveries of the archaeological excavations is the uncovering of a medieval church that might be the church that Grim Svertingsson built soon after Icelands conversion to Christianity. The church is 6 m long and 3 m wide. The excavation revealed the wooden frame that made up the church at Hrísbrú. Somewhat unusual in Iceland is the fact that this church was built from wood as a stave church rather than turf, which is the usual Icelandic building material. The remains of the church provide valuable information about medieval construction techniques. The architect Hjörleifur Stefánsson has drawn reconstructions of the church based on the information from the archaeological excavations. It remains uncertain, however, how the roof was constructed. The only sources about roof construction from this period are found in Hómelíubók (The Icelandic Book of Homilies), which speaks about the structural elements of the church and their religious significance.
